chapter_theme: Khechari yoga (கேசரி யோகம்): the tongue turned up into the palate and the breath held there make nectar flow from above, so that death, age and evil deeds lose their hold; the body becomes a lit temple where the Lord and Shakti dwell, and the yogi gains powers such as far sight.
structure_note: Sealing the body and turning the tongue up (799 to 809), the body as a temple and those who dwell in it (810 to 812), Shakti and the moon's kalas pouring nectar (813 to 816), raising and holding the breath (817 to 821), and far sight and the inner lamp (822 to 824). Many verses begin with the last word of the one before.

799.reading: So that nothing comes loose and drops down, bind the eight, bank the hearth, lock the crossbeam and fasten the upper bag at its stem; when one stays firm thus, there is no Yama.
799.nuance: The verse is a riddle in household words. அடுப்பு (hearth) is often taken as the fire at the base of the spine, மேற்பை (upper bag) as the head or the palate cavity, and what must not drop as the breath or the bindu; none of this is stated. The last line repeats 574.

800.reading: On the square plank where the washerman beats clothes, bank the edges so the channels do not leak, let the sky-river flow in and fill the tank, and on looking up one is free of dirt.
800.nuance: The plank is taken as the palate, the sky-river as the nectar from the head, and அண்ணாந்து பார்க்க (looking upward) as the upturned gaze or tongue. அழுக்கு may be bodily or the soul's impurity. Variants read விண்ணாற்றைத் தேக்கி and நிரப்பிட்டு.

801.reading: Those who exchange left hand and right and eat with the trunk need not grow weary; for those who can drive out sleep and stay aware, there is no need to die: they can remain.
801.nuance: Left and right hand are read as the two breaths, and துதிக்கை (an elephant's trunk) as the tongue turned back to 'eat' the nectar. The promise to stay without dying may be literal or may mean freedom from birth and death.

802.reading: If one practises with discernment, nectar wells up and stays; it speaks fittingly when its time comes; practised further it becomes the sphere of the moon, and flowing, it nourishes.
802.nuance: உரை செய்யில் recurs in each line and may mean 'practise' or 'utter', perhaps a mantra. The moon's sphere (நிலாமண்டலம்) is traditionally placed in the head as the source of nectar.

803.reading: If the tip of the tongue is pressed up into the middle, there the soul and Siva dwell; the three gods and the thirty-three appear, and the flesh does not die for a hundred crore of years.
803.nuance: நடுவே is taken as the cavity above the soft palate. சதகோடி யூனே is obscure; 'a hundred crore' may qualify the flesh's life or the gods. The verse places the soul and the Lord together in the body, as 725 does.

804.reading: On the peak of the high mountain where the body's juices flow, no one knows how the juice of the sky flows; for those who know it there is honey to drink, and clarity.
804.nuance: ஊனூறல் (flesh-juice) and வானூறல் (sky-juice) set bodily secretion against the nectar from above; the mountain peak is taken as the head. தெளியலு மாமே can mean 'one gains clarity' or 'one may drink it clear'.

805.reading: If the two breaths are set swiftly in the upper palate, there is no Death and the door opens; as the world sees, grey hair and wrinkles change and one becomes a child: by the command of supreme Nandi.
805.nuance: இரு கால் is read as the two breaths, and the door that opens as the opening at the crown. The last two lines repeat 734 almost word for word, where the means is union with a woman.

806.reading: Raising the tongue up, beginning from Nandi, and staying joined there, one rules the whole earth; those who sit thinking of the bound sun as outside them are doers of evil.
806.nuance: நந்தி முதலாக may mean 'with Nandi as the first' (invoking the teacher) or name a place in the body. Lines 3 and 4 are obscure; they may fault those who seek the light outside instead of within.

807.reading: Those who stood bewildered while evil deeds danced, if they seek the tongue, leave Yama no room; those who sought verse and saw its fruit through became sweet cane that danced the divine dance.
807.nuance: The rhymes நாவினை, பாவினை, தேவினை drive the verse more than its sense. பாவினை may be verse or sin; தீங்கரும்பு (sweet cane) sets up the next verse.

808.reading: Those whose practice is to make it sweet cane raise the tongue fully to its shoot there, and as they straighten the bent bud, the body's water comes rising like cane.
808.nuance: The cane image plays on கரும்பு and அரும்பு (bud). The bent thing straightened (கோணை நிமிர்த்திட) may be the curled tongue or the coiled kundalini; the verse does not say.

809.reading: Raise the tongue by the way of the body's water, drink the honey-water and say Sivaya nama; the way the breath's water comes will bring the Ganga: know well the way the sky's water comes.
809.nuance: சிவாய நம is the five-syllable mantra, here joined to the bodily practice. கானீர் is read as கால் நீர், water of the breath, and the Ganga as the nectar descending as it falls on Siva's head.

810.reading: For those who know it rightly and worship within, grace pours down as purified knowledge; entering and closing one door of the steps, knowing it within, the place of his dwelling becomes a temple.
810.nuance: Worship is moved inside the body. காய்ந்தறிவாக may mean knowledge burnt clean of impurity. The door (படிக்கதவு) recurs in 820; a variant reads கோய்ந்தறிந்.

811.reading: Those who make their home inside the temple are better than a mother to the whole world, good as ripe fruit even among those who are hostile to them, and worse than fire to doers of evil.
811.nuance: காயினும் நல்லவர் plays on காய் (unripe fruit, or to burn with anger): they are good even when bitter, or good even to those who burn against them. The verse makes the inward yogi a moral presence in the world, gentle and severe by turns.

812.reading: He is on the heads of the doers of evil, the golden abode of those who worship with flowers, within the devotion of those who sing verse, and in the minds of those of great deeds.
812.nuance: சென்னியிலுள்ளவன் (on the head) may mean he stands over evildoers as their judge, or that he is present even in them. பாகவத்து and மதி (mind or moon) can each be read more than one way.

813.reading: Like rays rising from the moon he is sixteen, and in the lord's house a hundred and a hundred and twenty-four; spreading his arrows within the house of motion, he remained without opposing.
813.nuance: The sixteen are taken as the moon's kalas; the other numbers and the houses (பதிமனை, கதிமனை) have no fixed reading. A variant replaces lines 2 and 3 with a different count.

814.reading: Shakti sat with those kalas around her; the maiden sat in their midst; she sat with a deer-like face shining like the moon; she sat pouring nectar.
814.nuance: கன்னி (the maiden) is a name of Shakti. The kalas are those of 813, so she is the moon in the head from which nectar flows. இருந்தனள் opens every line.

815.reading: The two silvers poured into the golden earthen enclosure flowed down and stayed within, beginning from the sky; for those who can guard what has gone so that it does not leave, it becomes a shoot.
815.nuance: Silver (வெள்ளி) is traditionally read as the white bindu or the nectar, and gold as the body or Shakti, as in the alchemical language of 834. The last line is garbled.

816.reading: When the tender creeper who is that quality stays there gladly as fragrance, the knowledge of the tattvas, which is wealth, stays with him as kin.
816.nuance: கோமளவல்லி (tender creeper) is a name of Shakti. Who 'he' is in இருந்தனன் is not said: the Lord or the yogi.

817.reading: The breath that rested will rise within; as this staff and the cosmos above are joined, if one makes it rise with that blossomed flower, the circle blossoms and one may live.
817.nuance: தண்டு (staff) is taken as the spine and அண்டம் as the head; the flower and the மண்டலம் may be a centre of the body. பரிந்த and பரிய are unclear.

818.reading: Seeing the mind's girdle within the circle, binding it below with intent, so that daylight shines in the vessel within, the one with ear-rings ceased his dance.
818.nuance: ஒட்டியாணம் (girdle) may point to the abdominal lock of hatha yoga (uddiyana). குண்டலக் காதன் (the one with ear-rings) is usually Siva, and his ceasing to dance is read as the stilling of movement; it may also be the jiva.

819.reading: The breath that is passing away will settle within, and the breath that is going out can be guarded; when it flows, at the time it scorns the round anklet, drive off the bag.
819.nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are plain; lines 3 and 4 are not. வட்டக் கழல் (round anklet) may be Siva's feet, and பை (bag) the body or a sheath.

820.reading: If one door of the steps is closed inside the bag, light will shine within the body; if the breath rises swiftly there, the temple daubed with black becomes lit with a gem lamp.
820.nuance: பை (bag) and மையணி கோயில் (a temple smeared dark, perhaps with soot) are read as the body, which held breath turns into a lamp-lit shrine. Which door is closed is not said.

821.reading: Willing the shining breath to rise, within the navel and in the throat where it is pressed, holding it so that the revered circle is gained, one can tell of what stood withering.
821.nuance: கும்பி is read as கும்பகம், holding the breath. A variant replaces line 2 with one naming காமம் and நாடி. The last line is unclear.

822.reading: One can speak of the breath and the sky, and of the hardness of earth and water; when these five come together, one can speak of seeing far.
822.nuance: The five are taken as the elements (earth, water, fire implied, air, sky). தூர தெரிசனம் (far sight) is one of the yogic powers. Lines 1 and 2 are marked corrupt in the source.

823.reading: I shall tell of far sight, and it can be seen: placing the dark-eyed one within in meditation and setting the mind on the lovely lamp, the whole earth is before one as in daylight.
823.nuance: காராருங் கண்ணி (the one with dark eyes) is taken as Shakti, and கடைன்யானம் as a garbled கடை தியானம் or ஞானம். Line 1 is marked corrupt.

824.reading: Twelve finger-breadths below the navel that rises first there is, they say, the daylight of the many Vedas; set a good lamp in the rising nada there and one becomes lord of the temple that arises in oneself.
824.nuance: முந்நால் (three fours) is read as twelve; whether the place is below or above the navel depends on how முன்னெழு and கீழே are taken. The body as a temple that rises within closes the chapter.

links.note: Both end on the same words, நட்டம் இருக்க நமனில்லை: in 574 after holding the breath by measure, in 799 after sealing the body for khechari. Tirumular gives the same promise to two practices.

The Kural says those who have gained the power of austerity can even leap past Death; Tirumular says Yama has no hold on the yogi who seals the body. Both make death conquerable, the Kural by austerity in general, Tirumular by a named technique.
The same closing lines, grey hair and wrinkles undone and the yogi made a child by Nandi's command, follow two different means: union with a woman in 734, the breath set in the palate in 805.
725 says Tirumular once held the body worthless, then found the Lord's temple inside it; 820 shows how that temple is lit, with held breath as its gem lamp.

Both call the body a bag (பை). The Naladiyar says it should be looked at as a bag turned inside out, a covered foulness to be shunned; Tirumular says that inside the same bag a light shines and it becomes a temple. The conflict holds if 820's பை is read as the body, as tradition takes it.

The Kural asks what worth is if one does not do sweet things even to those who harm one. Tirumular's inward yogis are good even to the hostile, but worse than fire to doers of evil, so their goodness has a limit the Kural's does not state.

source_issues: 813: a variant replaces lines 2 and 3 with a garbled reading (W\ற்றைம்பதோ டொன்றாய்), apparently a different count.
815: line 4 reads கொழுந்தது வாகுண்- குணமது தனே, garbled.
821: the variant for line 2 is garbled (நலண்-கிடுண்- காமத்து நாடியி Wள்ளே).
822 lines 1 and 2 and 823 line 1 are marked corrupt and carry stray f characters; 823 line 2 கடைன்யான is garbled.
